## 0. Inputs, conventions, and what is imported

Work over a characteristic-zero field k. H is locally Noetherian and carries the balanced tetragonal family of the theorem statement. Write p:C->H for the curve, h:=g^1_2 when C is hyperelliptic, D:=gamma^*O_{P^1}(1) the tetragonal divisor class of fibre degree 4, and L:=W_5 tensor omega^{-1}.

Imported as a **verified dependency**: ATT-0065 (subproblem C66-GEO-Z), confirmed independently by REV-0108 and REV-0109 (both verdict `confirmed` on every claim). I use exactly:

* CLM-0065-1: pi_*W, pi_*(W|_Gamma) locally free of ranks 26, 12 with arbitrary base change; Fit_0(coker phi)=I_12(phi).
* CLM-0065-3: the filtered snake reduction coker(phi)=coker(phi_5)=R^1pi_*(W_5(-Gamma)), no global splitting of W used (this is the form demanded by FND-0097/FND-0099 and by EXT constraints L18, L61).
* CLM-0065-4: Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e, compatible with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change, with the rigidified T-point criterion: a T-point of B factors through Z iff N_T is pullback from T, equivalently iff O(Gamma_T) is isomorphic to L_T tensor pi_T^*M_T for some invertible M_T on T.
* CLM-0065-5, CLM-0065-9: the canonical filtration with fibre degrees d_4=20, d_5=16 and the balanced ambient/intrinsic agreement.

Imported as **source-backed classical inputs**, used as stated and not reproved: Riemann-Roch and Serre duality on smooth proper curves; Clifford's theorem together with its equality case (equality for a special bundle A with 0<deg A<2g-2 forces C hyperelliptic); the classification of special complete linear systems on a hyperelliptic curve (the moving part of a special complete system is a multiple of g^1_2), which I re-derive in the form needed in Lemma 2; the CE structure theory for degree-four Gorenstein covers in the form of the resolution hypothesised in ATT-0065 and of the relative-canonical normalization O_X(1)|_C=omega_{C/P^1}; Grauert/constant-rank base change; the fact that a closed immersion of smooth S-schemes is a regular immersion; Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, Ch. 6 (refined Gysin maps for regular embeddings and the excess intersection formula).

Not imported, and not used anywhere: any statement from a repo attempt that is not a dependency of this task. Repo attempts ATT-0063 and ATT-0080 appear to assert a statement close to Proposition 1 below (via a Castelnuovo-Severi route rather than the linear-series route used here); they are **not** listed in `TASK.json.dependency_artifacts`, so nothing here rests on them and Proposition 1 is proved from scratch. I make no novelty claim for it.

Normalization used throughout: SRC-0004's convention W_f=(O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f))|_C with deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12-4f, so deg W_4=20, deg W_5=16, deg L=16-10=6; and the CE relative-canonical normalization O_X(1)|_C=omega_{C/P^1}=omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2) (degree 10+8=18, matching the packet's internal check 2(2g-2+4*2)=18), which gives W_5=omega_C^2 tensor gamma^*O(-1)=omega_C^2(-D) and hence

  L = omega_C(-D),  chi(L)=6-6+1=1,  h^1(L)=h^0(omega tensor L^{-1})=h^0(O_C(D)),  h^0(L)=1+h^0(D).  (0.1)

All assertions below are invariant under L -> L tensor p^*M: the incidence condition of CLM-0065-4 is stated up to such a twist, and P_{sub}(p_*L) is unchanged by it. This is the discipline required by EXT constraint L61.

## 1. Part (I): the rank ideals, and only two strata

This part is a step, not a novelty: FND-0122 already records I_11(phi)=I_5(phi_5)=O_B for the filtered balanced CE evaluation with six pairwise-disjoint sections. I reprove it because the argument below is used again in Part (IV), and because the hypotheses must be carried explicitly: EXT/primary constraint ("Assert Fit_0(coker phi)=I_12(phi)=I_6(phi_5) and I_11(phi)=O_B for an arbitrary base carrying a balanced family with any relative degree-6 divisor Gamma") blocks the statement for an *arbitrary* relative degree-six Gamma. Here Gamma is the tautological divisor of B=Conf_6(C/H), i.e. a sum of six pairwise-disjoint sections, exactly the ATT-0065 hypothesis, and the degree inequalities d_4-n=14>10=2g-2 and d_5-n=10=2g-2 hold.

By CLM-0065-1, phi is a map of vector bundles of ranks 26->12, so Fit_j(coker phi)=I_{12-j}(phi); in particular Fit_0=I_12 and Fit_1=I_11. By CLM-0065-4, Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e.

For Fit_1: by CLM-0065-3, coker(phi)=R^1pi_*(W_5(-Gamma)) canonically. R^1 of a relative curve is top-degree, hence commutes with arbitrary base change; so for every point b of B,

  coker(phi) tensor kappa(b) = H^1(C_b, W_5(-Gamma)_b) = H^0(C_b, omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma))^vee

by fibrewise Serre duality. The bundle omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma) has degree 10-16+6=0 on a genus-6 fibre, and a degree-zero line bundle on a smooth proper connected curve has h^0 in {0,1}. Hence dim_{kappa(b)} coker(phi) tensor kappa(b) <= 1 for every b. By Nakayama, coker(phi) is generated by at most one element in a neighbourhood of each point; therefore Fit_1(coker phi)=O_B, i.e. I_11(phi)=O_B. Since the minor ideals are nested, I_j(phi)=O_B for all j<=11. Consequently rank(phi_b) is 12 off Z and exactly 11 on Z: the determinantal stratification has exactly two strata, and there is no deeper rank drop to analyse. Formation of all of this commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change (Fitting ideals commute with arbitrary base change; the fibre bound is fibrewise).

The same computation on the reduced evaluation gives I_6(phi_5)=Fit_0(coker phi_5)=Fit_0(coker phi) and I_5(phi_5)=O_B.

## 2. Part (II): no h^0-jumping on the balanced locus

This is the part that discharges FND-0058 and answers the question FND-0104 leaves explicitly unsettled ("whether a non-primitive degree-4 pencil can have balanced CE splitting F=O(4)+O(5); this review does not settle that and does not assert the answer"), and it removes the obstacle recorded in ARCHIVE constraint L191.

Terminology, kept exactly as the primary constraints demand: *hyperelliptic-composed* means gamma=q o h with q:P^1->P^1 of degree two and h the hyperelliptic map, i.e. intermediate genus zero. I do **not** claim that constancy of h^0(L) is equivalent to excluding all non-primitive pencils: degree-four covers factoring through an intermediate curve of genus 1, 2 or 3 keep h^0(D)=2 and are harmless, exactly as the constraint records. Only the hyperelliptic-composed case must be excluded.

**Lemma 2.1 (hyperelliptic curves have no primitive tetragonal pencil).** Let C be hyperelliptic of genus 6 with hyperelliptic class h, and let gamma:C->P^1 be any degree-four morphism, D=gamma^*O(1). Then D is linearly equivalent to 2h, h^0(D)=3, and gamma=q o h for a degree-two q:P^1->P^1.

*Proof.* D is base-point-free (it is the pullback of a point class under a morphism) and deg D=4. By Riemann-Roch h^0(D)-h^1(D)=4-6+1=-1, so h^1(D)=h^0(D)+1>=3>0 and D is special. For a special complete system on a hyperelliptic curve the moving part is a multiple of h: writing |D|=|M|+F with M the moving part, M is again special (h^1(M)>=h^1(D)>0), and since M is special we may choose an effective N in |omega-M|, so |M| is the subsystem of |omega| of divisors containing N, i.e. phi_M is the composition of the canonical map with the linear projection from the span of N. For a hyperelliptic curve the canonical map is v_5 o h with image a rational normal quintic, so phi_M factors through h; being base-point-free, M=h^*O_{P^1}(m) for some m, i.e. M is linearly equivalent to m*h with h^0(M)=m+1. Since D is base-point-free, F=0 and D=M is linearly equivalent to m*h with 2m=4, so m=2, D is linearly equivalent to 2h and h^0(D)=h^0(2h)=3. Finally h^0(2h)=3=h^0(P^1,O(2)) and every section of O_C(2h) is a pullback along h, so the base-point-free pencil defining gamma is h^* of a base-point-free pencil of conics on the target P^1 of h, i.e. gamma=q o h with deg q=2. QED

(Consistency check of the same statement from the other side: for p not a Weierstrass point one has h-p=p' and hence 2h-2p=2p' is always effective, so |3h-2p|=|h|+2p' has base locus 2p' and never defines a degree-four morphism. The apparent family of "primitive" tetragonal pencils on hyperelliptic curves does not exist.)

**Lemma 2.2 (hyperelliptic-composed implies unbalanced).** With gamma=q o h as above, E=O(1)+O(4)+O(4) and h^0(P^1,F(-6))>=2; in particular F is not isomorphic to O(4)+O(5).

*Proof.* h_*O_C=O+O(-(g+1))=O+O(-7), and for a degree-two q one has q_*O(m)=O(floor(m/2))+O(floor((m-1)/2)); thus q_*O=O+O(-1) and q_*O(-7)=O(-4)+O(-4). Hence gamma_*O_C=q_*h_*O_C=O+O(-1)+O(-4)+O(-4), so E^vee=O(-1)+O(-4)+O(-4) and E=O(1)+O(4)+O(4) (deg E=9=g+3, as required).

Next, the relations bundle is the bundle of relative quadrics through C. Tensoring the CE resolution by O_X(2) gives 0->O_X(-2) tensor p_X^*det F->p_X^*F->I_C(2)->0; since R^i p_{X*}O_X(-2)=0 for all i on a P^2-bundle, p_{X*}(I_C(2))=F and R^1p_{X*}(I_C(2))=0. Pushing 0->I_C(2)->O_X(2)->O_C(2)->0 forward therefore yields the exact conic-bundle sequence

  0 -> F -> Sym^2 E -> gamma_*(O_X(2)|_C) -> 0,  O_X(2)|_C=omega_C^2 tensor gamma^*O(4).  (2.1)

Twist (2.1) by O(-6) and take sections; left-exactness alone gives

  h^0(F(-6)) >= h^0(P^1,Sym^2E(-6)) - h^0(C, omega_C^2(-2D)).

With E=O(1)+O(4)+O(4): Sym^2E=O(2)+O(5)^2+O(8)^3, so Sym^2E(-6)=O(-4)+O(-1)^2+O(2)^3 and h^0=9. With D=2h and omega=5h: omega_C^2(-2D)=10h-4h=6h of degree 12>2g-2=10, so h^1=0 and h^0=12-6+1=7. Hence h^0(F(-6))>=9-7=2. A balanced F would give F(-6)=O(-2)+O(-1) with h^0=0. QED

**Proposition 2.3 (constancy).** On every geometric fibre of a balanced family, C is non-hyperelliptic, h^0(D)=2, h^0(L)=3 and h^1(L)=2. Hence p_*L is locally free of rank 3 and R^1p_*L is locally free of rank 2, both commuting with arbitrary base change, over **any** locally Noetherian base, and Q:=P_{sub}(p_*L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle, smooth and proper over H of pure relative dimension 2, canonically identified with the relative Abel-Jacobi incidence (the functor of relative effective divisors Gamma' with O(Gamma') isomorphic to L up to a twist from the base).

*Proof.* If C were hyperelliptic then by Lemma 2.1 gamma is hyperelliptic-composed and by Lemma 2.2 F is unbalanced, contradiction. So C is non-hyperelliptic. Always h^0(D)>=2 (gamma^* is injective on H^0(P^1,O(1))). D is special (h^1(D)=h^0(omega-D)=h^0(L)>=chi(L)=1>0), so Clifford gives h^0(D)-1<=deg(D)/2=2, i.e. h^0(D)<=3, with equality forcing C hyperelliptic since 0<4<2g-2=10. Hence h^0(D)=2, and (0.1) gives h^0(L)=3, h^1(L)=2.

For local freeness over a possibly non-reduced base I do **not** invoke Grauert (which needs reducedness). Instead, R p_* L is represented by a two-term complex of vector bundles [K^0->K^1] of ranks r, r-1 (chi(L)=1); constancy of h^0=3 makes the map K^0->K^1 of locally constant fibre rank, so its kernel and cokernel are locally free (ranks 3 and 2) and commute with arbitrary base change. The identification of Q with the divisor functor is the standard one: a T-point of the divisor functor is a relative effective divisor Gamma' with O(Gamma') isomorphic to L_T tensor pi^*M; its canonical section is fibrewise nonzero, hence defines a line subbundle of (p_*L)_T tensor M, i.e. a T-point of Q, and conversely. Twisting by M does not change the point of Q. This is the compatible divisor/Abel-Jacobi construction demanded by FND-0047, FND-0107 and ARCHIVE constraints L190/L202; the *unqualified* Proj identification blocked there is not used, and it is now legitimate over the whole balanced base precisely because h^0(L) has been proved constant. QED

## 3. Part (III): every balanced |L_b| contains six distinct points

This discharges FND-0083 and the primary frontier obligation "nonemptiness of the reduced-support open in |L_b| and of the ordered Conf_6 incidence on every balanced geometric fibre". The blocked route ("conclude nonemptiness from chi(L)=1") is not used: chi(L)=1 gives only a possibly non-reduced member.

Fix a balanced geometric fibre; C is non-hyperelliptic of genus 6, deg L=6, h^0(L)=3 (Prop. 2.3). Write |L|=F+|M| with F the fixed divisor and |M| base-point-free, h^0(M)=h^0(L)=3.

**Step 1: F is reduced.** Suppose F>=2p. Then h^0(L(-2p))=h^0(L)=3 and A:=L(-2p) has degree 4; A is special (h^1(A)=h^0(A)+1=4>0 by Riemann-Roch), so Clifford gives 2=h^0(A)-1<=deg(A)/2=2, an equality with 0<4<10, forcing C hyperelliptic - contradiction.

**Step 2: deg F<=1.** M is special (h^1(M)>=h^1(L)=2>0), so Clifford gives 2=h^0(M)-1<=deg(M)/2, i.e. deg M>=4; if deg M=4 the same equality case forces C hyperelliptic. Hence deg M is 5 or 6 and deg F is 1 or 0. Combined with Step 1, F is either empty or a single reduced point.

**Step 3: the general member of |M| is reduced.** Since |M| is base-point-free of projective dimension 2, it defines a morphism phi_M:C->P^2 whose image Y is an integral curve spanning P^2 (the three sections are independent), and C->Y is finite and, char k=0, separable, hence etale over a dense open Y^o of the smooth locus of Y; Y\Y^o is finite. A hyperplane (line) H fails to be transverse to Y at a point of Y^o only if it belongs to the image of the projectivized conormal variety of Y^o, which has dimension (dim Y)+(2-1-dim Y)=1<2, a proper closed subset of the dual plane; and the lines meeting the finite set Y\Y^o form finitely many lines in the dual plane. So a general line meets Y transversally in deg Y distinct points of Y^o, and its pullback phi_M^*(line) is reduced because phi_M is etale over those points. (Char 0 is essential here, both for separability and for the dual-variety bound.)

**Step 4: assembling.** The members of |M| containing the at most one point of Supp F form a proper linear subspace of |M| (base-point-freeness), and by Step 3 the reduced members form a dense open subset of |M|. A member M' in the intersection of these two dense opens gives F+M' reduced of degree 6, i.e. six pairwise-distinct points. Hence U_b (the reduced-support locus of |L_b|) is nonempty, and being open in the irreducible P^2 it is dense. Its complement is nonempty: h^0(L(-2p))>=h^0(L)-2=1 for any p, so |L_b| contains a member non-reduced at p. Therefore U_b is a nonempty proper open subset of P^2, so it is **not** closed. This is exactly the two-witness form (a reduced member *and* a non-reduced member) demanded by EXT constraint L27; openness alone is not used to conclude non-closedness.

**Remark (why base-point-freeness cannot be assumed).** EXT constraint L55 suggests that passing to six distinct ordered points "requires base-point-freeness of L together with a Bertini-type genericity argument". Base-point-freeness of |L| is not available on the balanced locus and may genuinely fail: for a smooth plane quintic (genus 6, non-hyperelliptic) with canonical class 2H and tetragonal D=H-p one has L=omega(-D)=H+p with h^0(H+p)=h^0(H)=3, so p is a base point and |L|=|H|+p. Steps 1-2 are what replace base-point-freeness, and they are sharp: deg F=1 occurs, deg F>=2 does not.

## 4. Part (IV): Z is the ordering torsor; smoothness and fibre dimensions

Let D_univ be the universal divisor on Q (finite flat of degree 6 over Q by Prop. 2.3), let U be the open subscheme of Q over which D_univ->Q is etale (the complement of the image of the support of Omega_{D_univ/Q}; the formation of this open commutes with base change since D_univ->Q is finite flat), and let Utilde:=Isom_U({1,...,6}, D_univ|_U) be the associated scheme of orderings. Since D_univ|_U->U is finite etale of degree 6, Utilde->U is a finite etale S_6-torsor. **No reduction is applied to source or target anywhere**, which is what FND-0087 and EXT constraints L36/L37 require; and everything is stated on the (stack of) pairwise-distinct sections, not on coarse moduli, as FND-0075 and EXT constraints L58/L76 require.

**Proposition 4.1.** Z=Utilde as subfunctors of B=Conf_6(C/H), hence as H-schemes.

*Proof.* By CLM-0065-4 (confirmed in REV-0108/REV-0109), a T-point of B factors through Z iff the six disjoint sections x_1,...,x_6:T->C_T satisfy O(Gamma_T) isomorphic to L_T tensor pi^*M_T for some invertible M_T. Given such a T-point, Gamma_T=sum x_i(T) is finite etale of degree 6 over T (a disjoint union of sections), and by Prop. 2.3 it defines a T-point of Q, which lands in U because its universal divisor pulls back to the etale Gamma_T; together with the given ordering this is a T-point of Utilde. Conversely a T-point of Utilde gives a relative divisor in the linear system with etale support plus an ordering, i.e. six pairwise-disjoint sections with O(Gamma_T) isomorphic to L_T tensor pi^*M_T, i.e. a T-point of Z. The two constructions are mutually inverse and compatible with the maps to B, and Z is a closed subscheme of B, so the subfunctors coincide and Z=Utilde. QED

**Corollary 4.2 (fibre dimensions).** Z->H is smooth of pure relative dimension 2 (composite of the finite etale Utilde->U with the smooth relative-dimension-2 U->H, U being open in the P^2-bundle Q). It is surjective onto H: for every geometric point b of H, Part (III) supplies a reduced member of |L_b| and hence 720 ordered points of Z_b. Every geometric fibre Z_b is smooth of pure dimension 2 and is a finite etale S_6-torsor of degree 720 over the dense open U_b of |L_b| = P^2. Z is closed in B (it is a Fitting-ideal zero scheme), while U is **not** closed in Q (Part III); there is no conflict, the two ambients being different. If H is irreducible then Z has pure dimension dim H+2, and B=Conf_6(C/H) has dimension dim H+6, so Z has pure codimension 4 in B. Finally, since Z is smooth over H, the Fitting scheme structure defined by a_N^*I_e is reduced whenever H is reduced - a scheme-theoretic conclusion, not the geometric-points statement blocked by FND-0046 and by EXT constraints L47/L56/L74, and obtained only because ATT-0065 supplies the Fitting ideal itself.

No statement is made here about images in M_{6,6}: the primary constraint blocking "image dimension dim(B)+2" and FND-0120 (no quasi-finiteness of the forgetful map) both concern the image, whereas Corollary 4.2 is a statement about the source Z only.

## 5. Part (V): regular embedding, the excess bundle, and the Gysin map

Both Z and B=Conf_6(C/H) are smooth over H (relative dimensions 2 and 6), and Z is closed in B; a closed immersion of smooth H-schemes is a regular immersion, of codimension equal to the difference of relative dimensions. Hence:

  Z -> B is a regular embedding of pure codimension 4, with locally free conormal sheaf of rank 4.  (5.1)

This is derived from smoothness plus the conormal statement, **not** inferred from the numerology "expected 6 versus actual 4"; EXT constraint L28 and FND-0068 block the latter inference (in either direction), and FND-0068's observation that a locus below the expected determinantal codimension may nonetheless be cut out by a regular sequence of its actual codimension is here realized rather than assumed.

**The excess bundle.** e:H->P=Pic^0_{C/B} is a section of a smooth morphism of relative dimension g=6, hence a regular embedding of codimension 6, and Z=a_N^{-1}(e) with ideal a_N^*I_e (CLM-0065-4). Thus I_Z is locally generated by exactly 6 elements while ht I_Z=4: those 6 generators are never a regular sequence, and the discrepancy is measured by the excess. Concretely, on Z the sequence 0->T_{Z/H}->T_{B/H}|_Z->a_N^*T_e(P/H) is exact, so N_{Z/B} is the image of da_N and the excess bundle is Ex:=coker(da_N|_Z), of rank 6-4=2. Its identification: at a geometric point (p_1,...,p_6) of Z, da_N is the Abel-Jacobi differential (sum_i T_{p_i}C)->H^1(O_C), whose dual is the evaluation H^0(omega)->H^0(omega|_Gamma); the kernel of that dual is H^0(omega(-Gamma))=H^0(O_C(D)) (using O(Gamma)=L=omega(-D)), of dimension h^0(D)=2. Hence da_N has constant rank 6-2=4 along Z - an independent confirmation of (5.1) - and

  Ex = (p_*(omega_{C/H}(-Gamma))|_Z)^vee = (R^1 p_* L)|_Z (up to a twist by an invertible sheaf on Z),  rank Ex = 2 = h^1(L) = h^0(D).  (5.2)

So the excess identity recorded numerically in the working context (expected relative dimension 0 for the corank-one locus of phi_5 of ranks 11->6, i.e. expected codimension (11-5)(6-5)=6 in the relative Sym^6 of relative dimension 6; actual fibre dimension 2) is upgraded here to a canonical rank-two bundle. Note that the naive expected codimension (26-11)(12-11)=15 for the full phi is not the right bookkeeping, because the W_4 block of phi is everywhere surjective (deg W_4(-Gamma)=14>10); the honest expectation is the one computed from phi_5, and it gives excess 6-4=2.

**Gysin.** Since e is a regular embedding of codimension 6, Fulton's refined Gysin homomorphism e^! is defined for the morphism a_N:B->P with no hypothesis on Z. By (5.1) and (5.2) the excess intersection formula applies and gives

  e^![B] = c_2(Ex) cap [Z] in A_{dim B-6}(Z).  (5.3)

This is a Gysin statement for the pair (B,Z)=(Conf_6(C/H),Z) over the balanced base. It is **not** a Gysin statement for (M_{6,6},Z), which FND-0052 and ARCHIVE constraint L196 block and which is not claimed; nor does it carry any weight, purity or Tate information, which EXT constraint L69 and ARCHIVE constraints L200/L208 block and which is not claimed.

## 6. What is proved, what is imported, what remains

Proved here: Part (I) (reproof of the recorded FND-0122 statement, with hypotheses carried explicitly); Lemma 2.1, Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 2.3 (answering FND-0104's open question and discharging FND-0058 and ARCHIVE constraint L191); Part (III) (discharging FND-0083 and the primary frontier obligation on reduced-support nonemptiness, with the plane-quintic obstruction to the base-point-free route identified); Proposition 4.1, Corollary 4.2, and Part (V).

Imported and used as stated: ATT-0065 (CLM-0065-1/3/4/5/9) with REV-0108 and REV-0109; the classical inputs listed in Section 0.

Remaining, and explicitly not addressed: everything about M_{6,6} (image, closure, components, stabilizers, codimension, purity, Gysin, Hodge/Tate); the unbalanced CE strata, on which none of the above says anything; the emptiness or otherwise of any h^0-jumping stratum off the balanced locus; and the equation-bundle freeness hypothesis of ATT-0065, imported unchanged.

claims.justification: Section 1. Fit_j(coker phi)=I_{12-j}(phi) by CLM-0065-1; Fit_0=a_N^*I_e by CLM-0065-4; for Fit_1, CLM-0065-3 identifies coker phi with the top-degree R^1pi_*(W_5(-Gamma)), whose fibres are Serre-dual to H^0 of a degree-zero line bundle, hence of dimension <=1, and Nakayama gives local generation by one element. Hypotheses (six disjoint sections; d_4-n=14>10, d_5-n=10) are carried explicitly, as the working-context constraint on arbitrary relative degree-six Gamma requires. Not novel: FND-0122 already records this.
claims.statement: For the balanced (6,6) CE evaluation over B=Conf_6(C/H) with the tautological six pairwise-disjoint sections, I_12(phi)=Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e and I_11(phi)=Fit_1(coker phi)=O_B, hence I_j(phi)=O_B for j<=11 and the determinantal stratification has exactly two strata (rank 12 and rank exactly 11), stably under arbitrary locally Noetherian base change.

claims.justification: Lemma 2.1: D is base-point-free and special, the moving part of a special complete system on a hyperelliptic curve is a multiple of g^1_2 (canonical map factors through h, so phi_M does), base-point-freeness kills the fixed part, degree forces m=2, and H^0(2h)=h^*H^0(O_{P^1}(2)) makes the defining pencil a pullback.
claims.statement: On a hyperelliptic genus-6 curve, every degree-four morphism gamma to P^1 has gamma^*O(1) linearly equivalent to 2h with h^0=3, and factors as gamma=q o h with deg q=2; in particular a hyperelliptic genus-6 curve carries no primitive tetragonal pencil.

claims.justification: Lemma 2.2: gamma_*O_C=q_*h_*O_C=O+O(-1)+O(-4)+O(-4) from h_*O_C=O+O(-7) and q_*O(m)=O(floor(m/2))+O(floor((m-1)/2)); the CE resolution gives p_{X*}(I_C(2))=F and hence the conic-bundle sequence 0->F->Sym^2E->gamma_*(omega^2 tensor gamma^*O(4))->0; twisting by O(-6) and counting, 9-7=2.
claims.statement: A degree-four cover of P^1 by a hyperelliptic genus-6 curve has Tschirnhausen bundle E=O(1)+O(4)+O(4) and satisfies h^0(F(-6))>=2, hence is never balanced; equivalently no balanced tetragonal genus-6 fibre is hyperelliptic and none is hyperelliptic-composed. This answers the question left explicitly unsettled by FND-0104.

claims.justification: Proposition 2.3: CLM-0084-2 and CLM-0084-3 exclude the hyperelliptic case, Clifford with its equality case then forces h^0(D)=2, and chi(L)=1 with Serre duality gives h^0(L)=3, h^1(L)=2. Local freeness over non-reduced bases uses the constant-rank two-term perfect complex rather than Grauert; the divisor-functor identification avoids the blocked unqualified Proj identification.
claims.statement: On every geometric fibre of a balanced tetragonal genus-6 family, h^0(D)=2, h^0(L)=3, h^1(L)=2, with no jumping anywhere on the balanced locus; consequently p_*L and R^1p_*L are locally free of ranks 3 and 2 with arbitrary base change over any locally Noetherian base (no reducedness needed) and the relative Abel-Jacobi incidence is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle of pure relative dimension 2. This discharges FND-0058.

claims.justification: Section 3. Clifford's equality case excludes a doubled point in the fixed divisor (degree-4, h^0=3 would force hyperelliptic) and excludes deg F>=2 (same equality case for the moving part), so deg F<=1 and F is reduced; a char-0 dual-variety/Bertini argument makes the general member of the base-point-free moving part reduced, and base-point-freeness lets it avoid the single fixed point. Non-closedness uses both witnesses (a reduced member and a member non-reduced at p, from h^0(L(-2p))>=1), as EXT constraint L27 requires.
claims.statement: On every balanced geometric fibre, |L_b| contains a divisor with six pairwise-distinct points; the reduced-support open U_b is nonempty and dense in |L_b|=P^2 and is not closed. The fixed divisor of |L_b| is 0 or a single reduced point, and the base-point case genuinely occurs (plane quintics), so a base-point-freeness-plus-Bertini argument is not available.

claims.justification: Proposition 4.1, using the CLM-0065-4 rigidified T-point criterion in both directions together with the divisor-functor description of Q from CLM-0084-4. The etale locus U is an open subscheme whose formation commutes with base change, so FND-0087's reduction trap is avoided entirely.
claims.statement: Z=V(Fit_0(coker phi)) and the ordering torsor Utilde over the etale locus U of the universal divisor represent the same subfunctor of Conf_6(C/H), hence are equal as H-schemes; no reduction of source or target is used.

claims.justification: Corollary 4.2 from CLM-0084-6 (smooth composed with finite etale), CLM-0084-5 (surjectivity onto H), and closedness of a Fitting zero scheme. All statements are about the source Z over H, never about an image in M_{6,6}.
claims.statement: Z is smooth over H of pure relative dimension 2, surjective onto H, with every geometric fibre a smooth 2-dimensional finite etale S_6-torsor of degree 720 over the dense open U_b of |L_b|; Z is closed in Conf_6(C/H) (while U is not closed in the P^2-bundle Q); for irreducible H, Z has pure dimension dim H+2 and pure codimension 4 in Conf_6(C/H); and the Fitting scheme structure is reduced when H is reduced.

claims.justification: Section 5: a closed immersion of smooth H-schemes is regular; the Abel-Jacobi differential has corank h^0(omega(-Gamma))=h^0(D)=2 along Z, identifying Ex by relative duality; Fulton Ch. 6 supplies e^! and the excess intersection formula. The lci/Gysin conclusion is derived from smoothness and the conormal computation, not from the excess numerology, which EXT constraint L28 and FND-0068 block.
claims.statement: Z is regularly embedded in Conf_6(C/H) of pure codimension 4 with locally free rank-4 conormal sheaf; da_N has constant rank 4 along Z; the excess bundle Ex=coker(da_N|_Z) is canonically (R^1p_*L)|_Z up to a twist from Z, of rank 2=h^1(L)=h^0(D); and the refined Gysin homomorphism of the codimension-six regular embedding e satisfies e^![B]=c_2(Ex) cap [Z].

novelty_claims: Settles the question FND-0104 explicitly declines to answer - whether a tetragonal pencil composed with a hyperelliptic map can have balanced CE splitting - in the negative, and therefore proves that h^0(omega_C(-D))=3 is constant on the whole balanced locus, discharging FND-0058 and removing ARCHIVE constraint L191's obstruction to the relative P^2-bundle model over the entire balanced base.

Discharges FND-0083: every balanced geometric fibre's |L| contains a divisor of six pairwise-distinct points. The proof identifies and defeats an obstruction to the route sketched in EXT constraint L55: |L| need not be base-point-free on the balanced locus (smooth plane quintics with D=H-p give L=H+p with a base point), so base-point-freeness plus Bertini is unavailable; Clifford's equality case instead pins the fixed divisor to be 0 or one reduced point, and that bound is sharp.

Identifies the Fitting-determinantal incidence scheme Z functorially with the S_6-ordering torsor over the etale locus of the universal divisor, yielding smoothness over the base of pure relative dimension 2, closedness in Conf_6(C/H), reducedness of the determinantal scheme structure, and pure codimension 4 - a scheme-theoretic rather than geometric-point conclusion, and with no reduction applied to either side of the torsor.

Upgrades the numerical excess identity 6-4=2=h^1(L) to a canonical rank-two excess bundle (R^1p_*L)|_Z for a genuine regular embedding of codimension 4, with a refined Gysin formula e^![B]=c_2(Ex) cap [Z] over the balanced base; this realizes the possibility FND-0068 leaves open (below-expected codimension yet still cut out by a regular sequence of the actual codimension) instead of assuming either side of it.
summary: Computes the determinantal rank-drop ideals and all fibre dimensions of the balanced (6,6) CE evaluation, on top of the confirmed dependency ATT-0065 (REV-0108, REV-0109). Three things are settled that the packet records as open. First, FND-0104's explicitly unsettled question - whether a degree-four pencil composed with a hyperelliptic map can have balanced CE splitting - is answered negatively: on a hyperelliptic genus-six curve every degree-four morphism has gamma^*O(1)=2h and factors as q o h, whence E=O(1)+O(4)+O(4) and h^0(F(-6))>=9-7=2, contradicting balancedness. This makes h^0(L)=3 constant on the whole balanced locus and discharges FND-0058 and ARCHIVE constraint L191. Second, FND-0083's obligation is discharged: every balanced |L_b| contains a divisor of six distinct points. The proof is not the base-point-free Bertini recipe suggested by EXT constraint L55, which is unavailable because |L| can have a base point (plane quintics); instead Clifford's equality theorem forces the fixed divisor to be 0 or one reduced point and a dual-variety argument handles the base-point-free moving part. Third, the incidence Z is identified functorially with the S_6-torsor over the etale locus of the universal divisor, giving smoothness over H of pure relative dimension 2, closedness in Conf_6(C/H), a regular embedding of pure codimension 4 and an explicit rank-two excess bundle (R^1p_*L)|_Z, so the excess identity 6-4=2=h^1(L) becomes a bundle-level statement with a refined Gysin formula. The lci/Gysin conclusion is obtained from smoothness and a conormal computation, not inferred from the excess numerology, which EXT constraint L28 blocks. I_11(phi)=O_B is reproved but claimed as a step only, since FND-0122 already records it.

theorem_scope.base: arbitrary locally Noetherian scheme or algebraic stack over a characteristic-zero field carrying a balanced tetragonal genus-six family; no reducedness, irreducibility, smoothness or dimension hypothesis on H; all conclusions stable under arbitrary locally Noetherian base change
theorem_scope.characteristic: characteristic zero is used essentially in (III) (dual-variety/Bertini genericity and separability of C->image) and in the Clifford equality theorem
theorem_scope.generality: (I) holds verbatim under the ATT-0065 hypotheses (six pairwise-disjoint sections, d_4-n>2g-2, d_5-n=2g-2) and is NOT asserted for an arbitrary relative degree-six divisor; (II),(III) are statements about geometric fibres of the balanced locus at (g,n)=(6,6) and use the CE relative-canonical normalization; (IV),(V) are relative statements over H inside B=Conf_6(C/H) only
theorem_scope.not_covered: any assertion about M_{6,6}: image dimension, codimension, closedness, purity, components, stabilizers, quasi-finiteness of the forgetful map, Gysin for the pair (M_{6,6},Z), Hodge/weight/Tate type; unbalanced CE splitting types; non-reduced members and h^0-jumping strata (proved absent on the balanced locus, not analysed off it); emptiness or non-emptiness of the unbalanced strata; the ambient equation-bundle freeness hypothesis of ATT-0065, which is imported unchanged

theorem_statement: Let k be a field of characteristic zero and let H be a locally Noetherian k-scheme (or locally Noetherian algebraic k-stack) carrying a balanced tetragonal genus-six family: a smooth proper p:C->H with geometrically connected genus-6 fibres, a finite flat degree-four gamma:C->P^1_H with Casnati-Ekedahl (CE) embedding i:C->X=P_{P^1_H}(E^vee) whose ideal has the standard degree-four CE resolution 0->O_X(-4) tensor p_X^*det(F)->O_X(-2) tensor p_X^*F->I_C->0, and whose rank-two relations bundle F is balanced on every geometric fibre of s:P^1_H->H (F_b isomorphic to O(4) direct-sum O(5)). Let 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 be the canonical CE filtration of ATT-0065 (fibre degrees 20 and 16), L:=W_5 tensor omega_{C/H}^{-1} of fibre degree 6, B:=Conf_6(C/H) the ordered configuration space of six pairwise-disjoint sections with tautological Gamma, phi:pi_*W->pi_*(W|_Gamma) the CE evaluation of ranks 26->12 over B, N:=omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma), a_N:B->P:=Pic^0_{C/B}, and Z:=V(Fit_0(coker phi)) the closed evaluation-failure subscheme of B. Then, all statements being invariant under replacing L by L tensor p^*M for an invertible M on the base: (I) RANK IDEALS. I_12(phi)=Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e and I_11(phi)=Fit_1(coker phi)=O_B, hence I_j(phi)=O_B for all j<=11; the determinantal stratification of phi has exactly two strata, rank 12 on B\Z and rank exactly 11 on Z, over any locally Noetherian base and after arbitrary base change. (II) NO JUMPING. Every geometric fibre of the balanced family is non-hyperelliptic and its tetragonal pencil is not composed with a hyperelliptic map; consequently h^0(D)=2, h^0(L)=3 and h^1(L)=2 identically on the balanced locus, p_*L and R^1p_*L are locally free of ranks 3 and 2 commuting with arbitrary base change over ANY locally Noetherian base (no reducedness hypothesis), and the relative Abel-Jacobi incidence Q:=P_{sub}(p_*L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle, smooth and proper over H of pure relative dimension 2. (III) REDUCED MEMBERS EXIST. On every balanced geometric fibre, |L_b| contains a divisor of six pairwise-distinct points; the reduced-support open U_b of |L_b| is nonempty and dense, and its complement is nonempty, so U_b is a nonempty proper open subset of P^2 and is not closed. This holds although |L_b| need NOT be base-point-free on the balanced locus: the fixed divisor of |L_b| is either 0 or a single reduced point, the latter genuinely possible (smooth plane quintics with D=H-p have L=H+p with base point p), so a base-point-freeness-plus-Bertini argument is insufficient and a Clifford bound on the fixed part is required. (IV) FIBRE DIMENSIONS AND SCHEME STRUCTURE. Let U be the open subscheme of Q over which the universal divisor is etale, and Utilde the associated finite etale S_6-torsor of orderings (no reduction of source or target is taken anywhere). Then Z and Utilde represent the same subfunctor of B, hence Z=Utilde as H-schemes; Z is smooth over H of pure relative dimension 2, surjective onto H, closed in B=Conf_6(C/H) (while U is NOT closed in Q), and the Fitting scheme structure on Z is therefore reduced whenever H is reduced. (V) REGULAR EMBEDDING, EXCESS AND GYSIN. Z is regularly embedded in B with pure codimension 4 and locally free conormal sheaf of rank 4; da_N has constant rank 4 along Z; the ideal a_N^*I_e is locally generated by exactly 6 elements, which are therefore never a regular sequence, so the honest excess against the expected determinantal codimension 6 of the corank-one locus of phi_5 (ranks 11->6) equals 2, realized as the excess bundle Ex:=coker(da_N|_Z)^vee, canonically isomorphic to (R^1p_*L)|_Z up to a twist by an invertible sheaf on Z, of rank 2=h^1(L)=h^0(D); consequently the refined Gysin homomorphism e^! of the codimension-six regular embedding e:H->P exists and the excess intersection formula gives e^![B]=c_2(Ex) cap [Z] in A_*(Z). No claim whatsoever is made about the image, closure, dimension, codimension, purity, Gysin structure, weights or Tate type of Z or of its image in M_{6,6}.
